title: What can you say about maca in your ads and on your site?
summary: The library supports 3 wordings for maca; the strongest is "Helps support the emotional aspects of sexual health" (moderate, 3-3.5 g dried root a day). Avoid wording that names or implies a disease, a drug or a treatment, such as "Treats erectile dysfunction".

supported_wordings.wording: A source of antioxidants that help protect cells against damage from free radicals.
supported_wordings.why: Health Canada sets a maximum dose only; no other listed source covers it.
supported_wordings.daily_dose: up to 3 g dried root a day
supported_wordings.dose_details: Adults 18 and older, up to 3 g a day.

sources.name: Health Canada monograph: Maca - Lepidium meyenii

supported_wordings.wording: Helps support the emotional aspects of sexual health.
supported_wordings.why: Health Canada lists it at 3-3.5 g a day; no other listed source covers it.
supported_wordings.dose_details: Adults 18 and older; ask a practitioner for use beyond 6 weeks at more than 3 g a day.

sources.name: Health Canada monograph: Maca - Lepidium meyenii

supported_wordings.wording: Helps support a healthy mood balance during menopause.
supported_wordings.why: Health Canada lists it at 2-3.5 g a day; no other listed source covers it.
supported_wordings.dose_details: Adult women; ask a practitioner for use beyond 3 months (0.6-3 g a day) or 6 weeks (more than 3 g a day).

sources.name: Health Canada monograph: Maca - Lepidium meyenii

wordings_to_avoid.why: Names a mental health disorder; the supported wording is mood balance.

evidence_strengths.strong: At least two listed sources support it independently at a comparable dose and form, and none disagrees.
evidence_strengths.moderate: One listed source supports it as an evidence-based use at that dose, and no listed source disagrees.
evidence_strengths.limited: The only support is traditional use, the sources disagree, or the source itself calls the evidence weak.

reasons_to_avoid.drug: names a drug or presents the product as one
reasons_to_avoid.treatment: promises to treat, cure or prevent a condition

disclaimer: Not legal advice. This guide shows the wording that published evidence supports at a daily dose, from the sources linked below; it is not a ruling on any claim. Your own product, its form and dose, and your own evidence still need to match the wording you use.
